data.title: Project Rules
data.tagline: Repository-level instruction files that inject team stack requirements, coding conventions, and operational boundaries into an AI agent.
data.learningOutcome: You can put stable stack and approval rules in project instructions and distinguish them from client config and system prompts.
data.description: For example, a team can record its stack, code style, validation steps, and operating boundaries in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or another file supported by the tool. Whether it is loaded, which directories it covers, and its precedence are product-specific. Rules reduce repetition but do not guarantee compliance or replace permissions and tests.

learning.assumes: You collaborate with an AI agent on code inside a project.
learning.outcome: You can put stable stack and approval rules in project instructions and distinguish them from client config and system prompts.

distinctions.label: System Prompt
distinctions.explanation: A System Prompt shapes the model's fundamental persona and reasoning guidelines; Project Rules define repository-specific engineering conventions and workflow constraints.

explanation.title: Rules files contain conventions and constraints
explanation.text: A typical AGENTS.md or .cursorrules includes: (1) project overview and tech stack; (2) code conventions and structure; (3) forbidden actions (e.g. no committing, deleting DBs); (4) verification steps. Starting with 5–10 high-value rules works best.

explanation.title: Become part of the multi-turn context
explanation.text: Tools read project rules and pass them to the model automatically, reducing repetitive prompting.

explanation.title: Share rules with the repo, but never secrets
explanation.text: Team rules are committed to Git; real API keys and local paths belong in environment variables, not rules files.

data.boundary: Project rules guide the agent; they are not a client permission policy and do not prove correctness like a compiler, linter, or test. Keep sensitive actions inside permission boundaries, then verify changes with the project's checks and human judgment.

lessonPractice.title: The AI keeps generating code outside the team's stack. What is the most direct fix?

options.label: Put the stack, code style, and risky-action approval rules in project instructions
options.feedback: Correct. Project rules enter the agent's task context and guide generation toward the team's conventions.

options.label: Put code style rules in the client config that only controls the Provider and port
options.feedback: Client config controls how the tool connects and runs; it does not replace project guidance for the agent.

options.label: Only add compiler or linter checks and they will tell the AI how to write code before generation
options.feedback: Compilers and linters mainly catch problems after generation; they do not replace guidance during generation.

data.agentPrompt: Read the project rules before editing the button component. Follow the existing stack, do not use any, and ask before delete or reset commands. Run the project's existing checks after editing.
